editorNote: The week opens with Challenger on the pad and computer stores selling two futures at once: deeper games for home micros and fixed-disk IBM PC systems for offices.
morningLine: Computer Gaming World's May-June issue is arriving with modem gaming and baseball-league copy, while PC dealers keep explaining why a hard disk changes the office desk.

lead.headline: Modem games and baseball leagues reach the game rack
lead.dek: Computer Gaming World's May-June 1983 number put modem gaming, an adventure-games contest, and computer baseball league coverage in front of Apple II and strategy players.
lead.body: During the week of April 4-10, 1983, the liveliest personal-computer story was still at the game rack. Computer Gaming World Vol. 3 No. 3 carried cover lines for modem gaming, an adventure games contest, and a computer baseball league, with SSI strategy titles such as Knights of the Desert sharing space with reader-driven play. The shelf message was clear: home-computer games were becoming longer, more social, and more magazine-mediated than the arcade conversions beside them.
